messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: multiple OOM / CUDA errors observed on serving-rb-03 and serving-rb-05. 5xx rate increased ~2.3x in the last 12m. Investigate.

maria: seeing spiking OOMs on rb-03. logs show paged-allocator failing to reclaim KV pages, fragmentation creeping up.

ajay: confirmed. CUDA driver logs show out-of-memory on kernel launch, then container restart loop on rb-03. stack traces point to paged-attn allocator free path.

lee: how widespread? is this single node or whole AZ?

maria: primarily rb-03 and rb-05 in us-east-1a, a few fallback hits in us-east-1b when routing.

julia-sre: impact: a subset of hosted API keys hitting long context requests got 503s. SLO noise but not full region down yet. Customer-facing pages?

taylor: ops has 2 customers on dedicated pools in that cluster, low-volume but heavy long-history prompts. notifying success team.

ajay: quick mitigation options: 1) bump kvcache eviction frequency 2) enable strict prefix KV eviction policy per-pod 3) temporarily disable paged attention on affected nodes (fall back to non-paged path)

maria: we can toggle kvcache eviction via runtime flag. can push to rb-03 via deploy bot.

ops-bot: runbook command: `/cluster run --nodes rb-03 rb-05 --set runtime.paged_attention=false`

lee: careful — disabling paged attention increases memory, may push others to OOM. But it's faster to stop fragmentation path. prefer: tighten eviction + reduce max_seq_len for affected services to cut working set.

ajay: agree. plan: 1) set runtime.kv.eviction_rate=2x 2) set service.max_seq_len=1024 for public API routes on those nodes 3) enable fallback model routing to quantized-small for long requests.

maria: executing step 1 now. running command:

```
kubectl -n inference patch config runtime-config --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/kv/eviction_rate","value":"2"}]'
```

maria: patched eviction_rate. watching allocator metrics. fragmentation % dropping slowly.

ajay: pushed a canary for seq_len limit via route policy. reducing headroom; if we still see CUDA OOMs we'll scale pods out.

incident-bot: NOTE: 2 pods restarted in rb-03 in last 6m, reason: OOM_KILL.

lee: ops, can you cordon and drain rb-05 if it keeps flapping?

taylor: starting drain on rb-05; will redirect traffic off node. running: `kubectl cordon rb-05 && kubectl drain rb-05 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`

julia-sre: please capture `/proc/vmallocinfo` and allocator logs before pod termination if possible. create a tarball and drop to /tmp/incident-artifacts.

maria: collected logs and heap profiles from allocator. uploading to shared drive. link: https://redwood.infra/incident/1847500001/artifacts

ajay: digging into code — the paged-attn allocator has a slow-path race where freed pages can be marked as free but not returned to GPU due to refcount drift in the presence of preemption. suspect leak.

lee: any quick code hotfix?

ajay: can hotfix the free path to force deferred reclaim and periodic full sweep; will push patch to canary in 15m. minimal risk.

maria: customer impact update: only long-context requests from a handful of API keys hit 503. majority of traffic served by unaffected nodes. CS notified two accounts at risk.

ops-bot: Pager duty note: on-call handoff scheduled in 45m to lee. need handoff summary in thread.

maria: current mitigation state: eviction rate doubled, seq_len capped to 1024 on routes, rb-05 draining, hotfix in review to enable forced allocator sweep. error rate down from 2.3x to 1.1x.

ajay: pushed hotfix to canary on rb-01 (non-affected) for validation: `git rev-parse --short HEAD` -> `c3f9b2a`. Will promote to rb-03 after 10m if stable.

julia-sre: followups to create: 1) allocator stress test for paged-attn under preemption 2) add metrics for leaked refcounted pages 3) automated periodic defrag sweep 4) incident postmortem + customer timeline.

lee: noted. prepping handoff notes: will include current mitigations, artifact links, CS contacts, and rollout plan for hotfix.

maria: thanks all. if hotfix fails, fallback is to route long-context requests to smaller quantized model pool until patch is deployed.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: error rate stable. next update in 30m or on significant change. :white_check_mark:
